Numerical diagnostics · saved-data analysis · 19 November 2026

What happens after cycle 5?

The boundary spike is bad for the numerical reliability of the affected 3,072-level run. It means its finite basis is too small for some conditional states. It does not establish a physical five-cycle limit or identify a decoder defect. Average energy growth can occur under this measurement protocol, which has no energy stabilization; the abrupt rare jumps still need a controlled explanation.

New evidence: the 5,120-level follow-up completed. At cycle 8, its paired fidelity change relative to 4,096 is -0.128 percentage points, with 95% CI [-0.647, +0.390]. This supports cutoff stability of the average logical fidelity at the registered tolerance. It does not establish convergence of every trajectory, energy tail, measurement approximation, noise setting, or decoder.

The classical control has ideal encoding and classical readout. The replay arm applies its corrections to the finite-energy state without measurement backaction. These controls help expose protocol differences; their fidelity gaps do not isolate a single physical mechanism.

Inspect the rare trajectories

The selector contains the three trajectories with the largest peak boundary population in the 3,072-level run, selected by that rule before comparing cutoffs. They are diagnostic outliers, not representative samples.

PNG · SVG · Trajectory data CSV

For trajectory 1659 (initial X−), mean photon number jumps from 46.44 at cycle 5 to 2,602.07 at cycle 6 at N = 3,072. Its boundary mass reaches 94.99% at cycle 7. At N = 5,120 the same random-number index still jumps to 3,080.67 photons at cycle 6, while boundary mass remains below 0.061%. Thus a boundary failure and a high-energy event are separate observations.

Wrapped syndromes determine the nearest-lattice corrections here, so those curves also show the feedback commands. Common random numbers reduce comparison variance but do not enforce identical conditional measurement outcomes across cutoffs. Even at N = 5,120 this outlier's energy path is not shown to be converged.

A concrete measurement-approximation concern

The saved simulator evaluates the ancilla wavefunction by a piecewise-constant position-bin lookup. Sampling uses the matching bin density, so the two operations agree for that approximation. The jumps in the wavefunction nevertheless create artificial high-momentum components. This supplies a credible mechanism for rare high-energy events, not yet a demonstrated cause of the observed trajectory.

PNG · SVG

For derivative half-step h < dx/2:   ∫ |Dhφ|² dq = Σj|jumpj|² / (2h).

Panel B is a mathematical finite-difference diagnostic of the step-function approximation, not a measured physical momentum energy from these trajectories. For a continuous smooth resource this integral has a finite limit (about 31.83 in the nominal case). Panels C–D reuse a separate two-cycle refinement, 256 trajectories per input state, at N = 3,072. All nine pointwise fidelity comparisons pass its ±0.5 percentage point band; that short test does not resolve eight-cycle energy tails.

Root cause assessment

Candidate / observationEvidenceCurrent conclusion
Fock basis too small at N = 3,072Up to 94.99% probability reaches its top 10% of levels. Increasing N removes the boundary-gate failure through cycle 8.Confirmed numerical limitation for that cutoff. This explains why its affected results are unreliable, but not the origin of the high-energy event.
Measurement backaction and no energy stabilizationThe ensemble mean rises from 5.07 to 261.93 photons at N = 5,120 (average increase 32.11 per cycle); the replay arm has no comparable growth. The nominal smooth ancilla momentum variance is about 31.83.Consistent with expected heating under this protocol. The scale agreement does not prove the abrupt rare jumps are physical.
Piecewise-constant resource wavefunctionIts derivative-energy diagnostic diverges. Finer bins reduce boundary mass in the separate two-cycle study.Confirmed approximation defect for continuum energy; a plausible contributor to the spikes. Its causal contribution to this event is unresolved.
External displacement outlierFor trajectory 1659 at cycle 6: dq/√π ≈ 0.292 and dp/√π ≈ −0.121, versus stationary standard deviation 0.20.No large new applied displacement at the event. This does not rule out a conditional-state / measurement interaction.
Norm loss or logical extraction failureLargest norm error across the three runs is below 8×10⁻¹²; extraction trace error is below 4×10⁻¹¹.These diagnostics show no failure. Small norm/trace errors alone cannot certify physical accuracy.
LSTM or Bayes defectThis eight-cycle cutoff study uses the nearest-lattice controller only.No architecture-specific conclusion is supported by this study.

What would resolve the remaining uncertainty?

  1. Replace the bin lookup with a smooth analytic Mehler wavefunction and matching continuous outcome sampler; hold the physical protocol and decoder fixed. Validate it against the explicit two-mode reference before rerunning.
  2. Repeat the nominal eight-cycle comparison with the same noise and sampling budget. Compare fidelity, energy quantiles, rare jumps and boundary populations. Include a long-horizon bin-refinement control if retaining the binned implementation.
  3. For the outliers, record energy before/after displacement, q measurement, q feedback, p measurement and p feedback, plus unwrapped homodyne outcomes and their log probabilities. Saved round-end data cannot identify the first failing substep or the rarity of the full outcome.

Adding damping or energy feedback changes the physical protocol. It is a separate modeling experiment, not a numerical convergence fix. No new simulation or decoder training was launched for this review.

Metric definitions and reusable data

Logical fidelity
Overlap of the extracted logical state with its intended input state, averaged equally across ±X, ±Y and ±Z. Higher is better; 100% is perfect. Finite-energy encoding starts at about 97.72% before any cycle. This is not a classification accuracy or a per-round logical error rate.
Mean photon number ⟨n⟩
Energy of a conditional oscillator state, in photon-number units. The mean tracks the ensemble; median and 99th percentile describe its spread; the maximum exposes rare events. Higher energy needs a larger basis and can have a physical cost, but does not by itself imply a logical decoding error.
Boundary population
Probability weight in the highest 10% of Fock levels (a cutoff-dependent region). It is a warning diagnostic, not a decoder error probability. Registered gates require ensemble mean <0.01% and every trajectory <1%, in both arms, at every preceding cycle.
Paired cutoff difference and 95% interval
The average trajectory-level fidelity difference when the numerical cutoff increases. The entire pointwise interval must fit inside ±1 percentage point. This gate addresses mean fidelity at the tested cutoffs; it is not a universal convergence proof or a simultaneous confidence band.
Norm and extraction trace errors
Checks of state normalization and logical-observable quadrature completeness. They help catch arithmetic or integration problems; they can remain tiny while a finite basis or measurement approximation is inadequate.
